Lunch, high tea and dinner at the office, so the basics are taken care of while we build together. Learning & development credits to invest in courses, books, conferences and tools that help you get better at your craft. Relocation support to make moving closer to the team as seamless as possible. Great tools to do your best work, including high-spec equipment and software. An office designed for more than just work, with pickleball, table tennis, PlayStation, an arcade game room, an F1 simulator and even a full flight simulator. Our values shape how we make decisions, work together and build for travelers. The bar is high, the pace is fast, and the way we work is deliberate. Read them before you apply. Responsible GenAI usage: Explore responsible uses of GenAI to simplify analytical workflows, automate routine work and support insight generation while maintaining appropriate validation and oversight. Master's degree in Statistics or Economics, Data Science, Analytics or a related quantitative field. Ability to assess bias, assumptions, and limitations and explain whether results support a business conclusion. Advanced SQL and working proficiency in Python for statistical analysis and reusable workflows; experience with relevant libraries such as pandas, NumPy, SciPy or statsmodels and cloud platforms such as GCP or Azure. full_description: Description Are you passionate about giving customers the richest, most inspiring experience in their shopping journey? Do you like to dive deep to understand how customer-centric solutions drive measurable results? Do you enjoy working closely with the business and software engineers to design rigorous experiments, build the data infrastructure behind them, and translate results into decisions? You are in the right place! Come join our Prime & Marketing Analytics and Science (PRIMAS) team, where your work will directly impact millions of customers. The EU Marketing & Prime organization is looking for a Data Scientist to join the PRIMAS team. This role sits at the intersection of applied statistics and large-scale analytics — you'll design experiments and causal models, and also own the data pipelines, metrics, and reporting infrastructure that make those results usable across the business. The PRIMAS team provides a comprehensive understanding of customer segments, affinities, and lifetime value. We use data science tools and advanced statistical techniques to study customer purchase and engagement behaviors, and generate actionable insights on where, when, and how we deliver products and programs to customers. We help increase customer engagement, sales, and marketing efficiency, and our systems are built entirely in-house on automated large-scale analytics infrastructure. You will design, launch, and measure experiments across marketing channels (SEM/SEO, Affiliates, Display, Social, Mobile, Email, Onsite, etc.), engagement products, and customer segments. You will improve our understanding of customer behavior, run rigorous power and minimum detectable effect (MDE) analyses to size experiments correctly, and build the causal and conversion models that value and target our marketing — then build the pipelines and dashboards that keep those signals flowing reliably to stakeholders and downstream systems. You will work at the forefront of consumer analytics, tackling some of the hardest measurement problems in the industry alongside strong scientists, statisticians, and software engineers. Key job responsibilities Design and implement scalable, statistically rigorous experiments (A/B, geo, holdout, quasi-experiments) to measure marketing incrementality across channels. Perform power analysis and minimum detectable effect (MDE) calculations to determine experiment sample sizes, durations, and design trade-offs before launch. Build causal and treatment-effect models that produce conversion and valuation signals consumed by downstream bidding and budgeting systems. Building the ETL, metric definitions, and datasets that make results scalable, extensible, and repeatable rather than one-off analyses. Develop measurement frameworks that quantify the true, platform-independent contribution of marketing over time, and build the dashboards and reporting that keep those metrics visible to the business. Apply statistical, mathematical, and machine learning techniques to solve ambiguous business problems where the right approach isn't obvious. Analyze experiment results for validity — inspecting distributions, checking for sample ratio mismatch, exploring covariate balance, and tracking down the source of anomalies. Communicate experiment design, results, and trade-offs clearly to business and leadership audiences, including inputs into business reviews, and influence decisions and technical direction across teams. Establish scalable, repeatable processes and best practices for experiment design, data modeling, and analysis. Basic Qualifications 4+ years of data scientist experience 4+ years of machine learning, statistical modeling, data mining, and analytics techniques experience 4+ years of data querying languages (e.g. SQL), scripting languages (e.g. Python) or statistical/mathematical software (e.g. R, SAS, Matlab, etc.) experience 1+ years of working with or evaluating AI systems experience Experience applying theoretical models in an applied environment Experience writing complex SQL queries Preferred Qualifications Master's degree in Science, Technology, Engineering, or Mathematics (STEM) Knowledge of machine learning concepts and their application to reasoning and problem-solving Experience in a ML or data scientist role with a large technology company Experience in defining and creating benchmarks for assessing GenAI model performance Experience working on multi-team, cross-disciplinary projects Experience applying quantitative analysis to solve business problems and making data-driven business decisions Experience effectively communicating complex concepts through written and verbal communication Our inclusive culture empowers Amazonians to deliver the best results for our customers. Risk Consulting – Financial Services Risk Management (FSRM) – Basel III Business Analyst – Manager/Senior Description EY's Financial Services Office (FSO) is a unique, industry-focused business unit that provides a broad range of integrated services that leverage deep industry experience with strong functional capability and product knowledge. FSO practice provides integrated consulting services to financial institutions and other capital markets participants, including commercial banks, investment banks, broker-dealers, asset managers (traditional and alternative), insurance and energy trading companies, and the Corporate Treasury functions of leading Fortune 500 Companies. The service offerings provided by the FSO Consulting include: market, credit and operational risk management, regulatory consulting, quantitative consulting, structured finance transaction, actuarial consulting, technology enablement, risk and security, program consulting, and process & controls. Within EY’s Business Consulting Practice, the Financial Services Risk Management (FSRM) group provides solutions that can help FSO clients to identify, measure, manage and monitor the market (trading book), credit (banking book), operational, and regulatory risks associated with their trading, asset-liability management, capital management and other capital markets activities. Within FSRM, the CSTC team assists across end-to-end aspects of Capital management, BASEL, credit risk and Stress testing related activities: Key role involves producing critical deliverables to the senior management and regulators including EMEIA, US and APAC entities’ credit risk review, capital projections, Basel 4, Basel 3 endgame, capital aspects of Recovery & Resolution planning (RRP), stress testing and having oversight of various regulatory requirements. Consulting and solutions delivery such as impact assessments, defining the target operating model, and integrated risk and finance reporting framework Quality assurance such as assessment of controls of the Banking industry and similar business lines covering regulatory reporting involving Basel/CRR/RRP regulations Early identification and accurate analysis of prudential developments and influence on changes to the capital framework. Regulatory capital impact assessment in legal entity simplification initiatives, business re-organizations, new business initiatives and external commitments to regulators Clients include large domestic and global financial institutions, broker-dealers, foreign banking organizations, asset management firms with significant capital markets activities. Project teams frequently work with the senior management of these firms, including CFOs and CROs. Role Overview The role is for a Basel III Business Analyst supporting the Basel III Proposal Roadmap implementation. The engagement focuses on restarting Basel III Proposal implementation program, adopting the Expanded Risk-Based Approach (ERBA), accelerating Single Counterparty Credit Limits (SCCL) gross exposure measurements, and onboarding incremental Basel III data requirements into the Unified Consumption Layer (UCL) Data Factory. The candidate will support exposure-pod based execution across credit risk, securitization, credit risk mitigation, derivatives / SA-CCR, operational risk, and related regulatory capital workstreams. The role requires strong business analysis, regulatory capital, data sourcing, data profiling, source-to-target mapping, calculation logic documentation, Axiom input mapping, controls design, testing, governance, and stakeholder management capabilities. The candidate will work closely with Risk, Finance, Technology, Data, Operations, and business stakeholders to produce implementation-ready requirements, support interim ERBA calculator development, and enable transparent program execution through high-quality documentation, testing, and governance routines. Key Responsibilities Support detailed implementation planning, governance, project management, status reporting, RAID / action trackers, decision logs, and senior stakeholder updates for the B3P Roadmap. Refresh the Basel III Proposal / ERBA gap assessment and identify new, modified, or enhanced data elements required for rule interpretation, regulatory capital calculations, and downstream reporting. Perform data profiling and fit-for-use analysis across existing UCL data elements and source-system data, including review of missing values, syntax consistency, data completeness, appropriateness for regulatory requirements, and data quality issues. Document data sourcing, transformation, derivation, and calculation logic requirements for ERBA exposure types including residential mortgage / MSR, CRE, retail, off-balance sheet, corporates, banks, securitization, credit risk mitigation, collateral haircut approach, derivatives / SA-CCR, and operational risk. Develop source-to-target mappings, business data dictionaries, data lineage, and transformation specifications to support onboarding of incremental Basel III data requirements into the UCL Data Factory. Support UCL Data Factory activities, including data movement logic, UCL data model design, legacy consumption views, UCL ADRS unification, semantic layer configuration inputs, and source-to-target reconciliation / data validation activities. Map data elements to Axiom-required calculation inputs and document the business rules, derivations, assumptions, controls, and evidence required to support regulatory capital processing. Assist in the design, build, and testing of interim ERBA calculators using available UCL data and direct source-system data until strategic UCL feeds are available. Support testing of calculator outputs, reconciliation of data and results, fit-for-use analysis, issue identification, remediation tracking, and user acceptance testing using project accelerators and agreed testing approaches. Identify and document controls for new or modified data elements, including preventative and detective controls, data quality checks, lineage controls, reconciliation points, and governance documentation. Recommend interim and strategic BAU data capture, data management, and process enhancements to support ERBA, SCCL gross exposure measurements, regulatory reporting, management reporting, and future-state capital insights. Coordinate with exposure pods, technology teams, and business stakeholders to drive agile execution across discovery, assessment, design, build, testing, and refinement sprints. Prepare clear, executive-ready documentation including requirements packs, mapping documents, control matrices, testing summaries, issue trackers, status decks, and steering committee materials. Responsibly use AI and automation tools to improve analysis, documentation quality, workflow efficiency, and delivery transparency while following engagement and client requirements. Qualifications, Certifications And Education Must-have: Master’s degree in business administration, finance, economics, engineering, statistics, information systems, or a related discipline, with at least 5 years of relevant experience in banking, consulting, risk management, regulatory capital, data management, or regulatory reporting. Strong understanding of Basel III / Basel III Endgame / Basel III Proposal requirements, ERBA concepts, RWA calculations, regulatory capital, credit risk, counterparty credit risk, operational risk, and regulatory reporting processes. Experience supporting Basel implementation, gap assessments, regulatory capital transformation, data sourcing, calculation logic documentation, data quality remediation, or regulatory reporting change programs. Strong business and data analysis skills, including requirements documentation, data profiling, source-to-target mapping, data lineage, data dictionaries, metadata management, reconciliation, and control documentation. Ability to understand exposure-level requirements across residential mortgage, CRE, retail, off-balance sheet exposures, corporates, banks, securitization, credit risk mitigation, SA-CCR, and operational risk. Experience working with senior stakeholders across Risk, Finance, Credit, Technology, Data, Operations, Compliance, and business teams in a structured and professional manner. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with ability to translate regulatory requirements into practical data, logic, controls, testing, and implementation deliverables. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with proficiency in preparing executive-ready PowerPoint materials, Excel trackers, meeting notes, governance reports, requirements documents, and testing summaries. Demonstrated focus on delivery excellence, attention to detail, process discipline, documentation quality, stakeholder management, and continuous improvement. Good-to-have: Experience with Axiom, regulatory capital calculators, RWA engines, regulatory reporting platforms, or capital data warehouses. Technical skills such as SQL, SAS, Python, advanced Excel, data profiling tools, data visualization tools, or cloud data platforms such as Snowflake, Azure, GCP, or similar environments. Familiarity with UCL / data factory delivery concepts, source-to-target reconciliation, consumption views, semantic layers, data model design, ADRS unification, and ETL design documentation. Familiarity with SA-CCR, SCCL, credit risk mitigation, collateral haircut approach, securitization capital rules, corporate / wholesale banking products, and operational risk SMA / BIC concepts. Certifications such as FRM, CFA, PRM, PMP, PRINCE2, Agile / Scrum, DAMA, or other relevant risk, data, or project delivery credentials. Hands-on experience with project management, collaboration, and reporting tools such as MS Project, Jira, Confluence, SharePoint, Power BI, Tableau, or similar platforms. Prior consulting experience or experience working with US banks, regional banks, global financial institutions, or regulatory-driven change and remediation programs. Enabled by data and technology, diverse EY teams in over 150 countries provide trust through assurance and help clients grow, transform and operate. full_description: ROLE OVERVIEW We are seeking an experienced SAP Oil & Gas Functional Business Analyst to act as the functional bridge between the business, SAP delivery teams and our UiPath Test Automation Engineers. Prepare and maintain functional documentation (process flows, business process maps, data dependency matrices and transaction guides) tailored for an automation audience. Respond to day-to-day functional queries from the automation team and resolve ambiguity quickly to keep automation development on schedule. Test Scenario Design & Automation Support Analyse business requirements, functional specifications and process designs to identify critical test scenarios across business-as-usual, exception and edge cases. Define and document detailed test scenarios, test cases, preconditions, test data requirements and expected results in a format suitable for automation. Partner with automation engineers to prioritise processes for automation based on business criticality, transaction volume, change frequency and regression risk. Review automated test cases and UiPath workflows for functional accuracy, ensuring they validate the right business outcomes, postings and document flows. Identify and help prepare reusable, stable test data sets (materials, customers, vendors, contracts, plants, storage locations, pricing conditions) and advise on data refresh and dependency strategies. Support defect triage by distinguishing automation script failures from genuine functional defects, and liaise with SAP functional and development teams to resolve issues. Integration & End-to-End Process Coverage Map and explain integration points between SAP Oil & Gas and core SAP modules (SD, MM, FI/CO, PM, QM, PP, EWM) as well as external systems such as terminal automation, SCADA, hydrocarbon accounting, pricing and third-party logistics platforms. Design end-to-end test scenarios that span multiple modules and interfaces (IDocs, BAPIs, RFCs, APIs, middleware such as SAP PI/PO or SAP Integration Suite), validating data flow and reconciliation across systems. Ensure automated regression packs adequately cover high-risk integration touchpoints, financial postings and month-end processes. Stakeholder Collaboration & Governance Work with Business Process Owners and key users to validate test scenarios and obtain sign-off on functional coverage. Assess the impact of SAP releases, support packs, enhancements and change requests on existing automated test suites, and advise on required updates. Promote best practices in requirement traceability, linking business requirements to test cases and automation coverage within the test management tool. REQUIRED FUNCTIONAL EXPERTISE: SAP OIL & GAS Strong hands-on knowledge across several of the following SAP Oil & Gas areas is required: Downstream HPM: Hydrocarbon Product Management (HPM), covering dual units of measure, temperature and density conversions, quantity conversion logic. Transportation & Distribution (TD): Bulk transport planning, shipment scheduling, load confirmation and delivery confirmation processes. Trader's & Scheduler's Workbench (TSW): Stock projection, nominations, bulk scheduling and ticketing. Exchanges: Exchange agreements, borrow/loan, netting and exchange settlement. Pricing: Formula-based and quotation-based pricing, marketing pricing and price determination. Inventory & Excise: Tank and silo management, physical inventory, gain/loss handling and excise duty processes. Retail & Secondary Distribution: Service Station Retailing (SSR) and Secondary Distribution (SAP OGSD), where applicable. Upstream (desirable) Joint Venture Accounting (JVA), including cost allocation, cutback and partner billing. Production and Revenue Accounting (PRA) and/or Upstream Operations Management (UOM). Core SAP Integration Sound understanding of Order-to-Cash, Procure-to-Pay, Plan-to-Produce and Record-to-Report processes as they apply to Oil & Gas. Working knowledge of how Oil & Gas transactions drive financial postings and controlling objects in FI/CO. REQUIRED SKILLS & EXPERIENCE Experience: 8–12 years of overall SAP functional experience, with a minimum of 5 years focused on SAP Oil & Gas (IS-Oil and/or S/4HANA for Oil & Gas). Delivery: At least 2 full-lifecycle SAP implementations, rollouts or large support engagements within the Oil & Gas industry. Testing: Proven experience supporting testing activities (SIT, UAT and regression testing), including test scenario design and test data preparation. Automation: Experience working with test automation teams; exposure to UiPath Test Suite (Studio, Test Manager, Orchestrator) or comparable tools (Tricentis Tosca, Worksoft, SAP CBTA) is strongly preferred. Communication: Ability to explain complex business processes clearly to technical audiences who may not have an SAP or Oil & Gas background. Analytical: Strong analytical, documentation and problem-solving skills with keen attention to detail. Tools: Familiarity with SAP Solution Manager, SAP Cloud ALM, Jira, Azure DevOps or similar tools for requirements and defect management. Methodology: Experience working within Agile/Scrum and hybrid delivery models. PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Information Technology, Business Administration or a related field; an MBA is an advantage. SAP certification in a relevant functional area (SD, MM, FI/CO) or SAP Oil & Gas. Understanding of RPA concepts and automation design principles such as modular, reusable and data-driven test design. KEY COMPETENCIES Business process thinking with an end-to-end view of Oil & Gas value chains. Collaborative, coaching-oriented approach to working with technical teams. Ownership, accountability and the ability to work independently with minimal supervision. Clear, structured written and verbal communication with stakeholders at all levels. Adaptability in fast-paced, multi-vendor and geographically distributed environments. WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE UiPath Test Automation Engineers are fully enabled to understand and automate SAP Oil & Gas processes with minimal rework. Automated regression suites provide comprehensive, functionally accurate coverage of critical business workflows and integration points. Functional defects are identified earlier in the lifecycle, reducing production incidents and release risk. Test scenarios, data and documentation are well structured, traceable and maintainable over successive SAP releases.

full_description: LOCATIONS Atlanta Chicago New York DEPARTMENT CFO Technology Company Overview We are the better way to work in finance. Through financial consulting rooted in data, technology, and AI, we help clients drive value—supporting the office of the CFO to drive end-to-end value creation. Backed by premier private equity firms and headquartered in New York with 11 offices around the globe, we are a high-growth, entrepreneurial firm looking for people who want to be part of building something great. Come make your mark. CFO Technology Accordion’s CFO Technology Practice effectively and efficiently delivers the digital services and solutions to support organizational strategic initiatives. Our CFO Technology experts work cross-functionally — alongside practitioners from all corners of Accordion — to arm CFOs with the appropriate digital solutions needed to implement the team’s business process recommendations and to capitalize on value creation opportunities. From ERP, CPM, Analytics, Data Integration, RPA, and beyond, CFO Tech provides finance leaders with a single, objective partner capable of delivering from strategy to execution. This role can be based in any of our US office locations and is a hybrid role with the flexibility to work remotely 2 days a week. Ideal candidates should be local to the desired location. This position is not eligible for immigration sponsorship. Overview Accordion is seeking a Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) to embed directly with client finance teams and build AI-powered agents and automated workflows that transform how organizations interact with their Enterprise Performance Management (EPM) and Corporate Performance Management (CPM) systems. Rather than implementing the platforms themselves, this role focuses on creating intelligent solutions—such as FP&A variance analysis agents, close reporting agents, forecasting co-pilots, and automated data reconciliation workflows—that sit on top of existing financial systems and dramatically accelerate the speed and quality of financial decision-making. The FDE will work at the intersection of applied AI, financial domain expertise, and client delivery—understanding the nuances of each client’s financial architecture, identifying high-value automation opportunities, and shipping production-grade AI agents that become embedded in the client’s day-to-day finance operations. Key Responsibilities AI Agent Development and Deployment Design, build, and deploy AI agents tailored to client-specific financial workflows, including variance analysis agents that automatically surface and explain P&L and balance sheet movements, close reporting agents that generate narrative commentary and executive summaries, and forecasting co-pilots that assist FP&A teams with scenario modeling and assumption validation. Build integrations between AI agents and existing EPM/CPM platforms (e.g., Oracle EPM Cloud, OneStream, Anaplan, Planful, Workday Adaptive Planning) to read from and write back to the client’s system of record. Develop automated data reconciliation and validation workflows that reduce manual effort during period-end close, intercompany eliminations, and management reporting cycles. Implement retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipelines, tool-use patterns, and multi-step agent architectures that ground AI outputs in the client’s actual financial data and business context. Client Discovery and Solution Design Embed with client finance, FP&A, and accounting teams to deeply understand their existing EPM/CPM environment, data flows, reporting cadences, and pain points. Identify and prioritize high-impact opportunities where AI agents and automation can eliminate manual, repetitive work—particularly in variance commentary, flux analysis, board reporting, cash flow forecasting, and data quality assurance. Translate business requirements into technical solution architectures, defining agent capabilities, data source integrations, guardrails, and success metrics in collaboration with client stakeholders. Manage the full lifecycle of agent development on-site—from rapid prototyping and stakeholder demos through iteration, testing, deployment, and post-launch monitoring. Platform and Product Thinking Contribute to Accordion’s reusable agent framework and shared component library, abstracting patterns from client engagements into configurable, scalable building blocks for future deployments. Stay current on advances in large language models, agent frameworks (e.g., LangChain, LangGraph, CrewAI, Anthropic tool use), and emerging best practices for building reliable, auditable AI systems in financial contexts. Establish and enforce quality standards for AI outputs in financial workflows, including accuracy validation, hallucination mitigation, audit trail generation, and appropriate human-in-the-loop checkpoints. Document solution architectures, integration patterns, and deployment playbooks to accelerate future client engagements and enable knowledge transfer across the team. Required Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Data Science, Finance, or a related field. 3+ years of software engineering experience, with at least 1 year focused on building applications powered by large language models, AI agents, or intelligent automation. Strong proficiency in Python and experience with LLM orchestration frameworks (e.g., LangChain, LangGraph, Anthropic API, OpenAI API) and related tooling (vector databases, embedding models, prompt engineering). Working knowledge of financial processes including budgeting, forecasting, financial consolidation, close management, variance analysis, and management reporting. Solid SQL skills and experience integrating with APIs, data warehouses, ERPs, and financial systems to source and transform data for AI workflows. Excellent communication skills with the ability to work directly with CFOs, controllers, and FP&A leaders—translating their needs into technical solutions and demonstrating value through rapid iteration. Willingness to travel to client sites as needed (up to 50–80%, depending on engagement). Preferred Qualifications Understanding of financial planning and reporting systems (Oracle EPM Cloud, OneStream, Anaplan, Planful, Workday Adaptive Planning) Experience in consulting or professional services. Familiarity with ERP systems (NetSuite, SAP, Oracle EBS, Microsoft Dynamics) and how financial data flows from transactional systems into EPM/CPM platforms. Experience building production AI systems with appropriate guardrails for regulated or audit-sensitive environments, including explainability, traceability, and human-in-the-loop review patterns. Cloud infrastructure experience (AWS, Azure, GCP) and comfort deploying and monitoring agent-based applications in production environments. Background in financial data modeling, multidimensional databases, or business intelligence tooling. Example Agent Use Cases The following are illustrative examples of the kinds of AI agents and workflows this role would build for clients: Agent / Workflow Description FP&A Variance Analysis Agent Automatically pulls actuals vs. budget/forecast from the EPM system, identifies material variances, drills into driver-level detail, and generates narrative explanations ready for management review. Close Reporting Agent Monitors close task completion, assembles period-end financial packages, generates board-ready commentary, and flags anomalies or incomplete items to the controller. Forecast Co-Pilot Assists FP&A analysts with scenario modeling by ingesting historical trends, suggesting assumption ranges, stress-testing inputs, and summarizing sensitivity analysis in plain language. Data Reconciliation Workflow Automatically reconciles data between the ERP, EPM, and reporting layers, identifies discrepancies, classifies root causes, and routes exceptions for human review. Consolidation Audit Agent Reviews intercompany eliminations and consolidation adjustments, validates entity-level roll-ups against source data, and produces an audit-ready exception report with supporting detail. What Success Looks Like In the first 90 days, a successful Forward Deployed Engineer will have embedded with at least one client, mapped their financial system landscape and key pain points, and delivered a working prototype of an AI agent that addresses a concrete workflow bottleneck. Within six months, the FDE will have deployed production agents that are actively used by the client’s finance team, measurably reducing manual effort in areas like variance analysis or close reporting, and will be contributing reusable components back to Accordion’s agent platform. RL of LLMs for security use cases as a post-training or continual learning process. Track the research literature, reproduce relevant results, and assess new methods for adoption. Document results, negative as well as positive, to support internal decision-making. title: Lead Engineer, AI Platform

full_description: About Us Circle is building the world’s leading AI-powered, all-in-one platform for digital businesses. We make it possible for creators, coaches, educators, and businesses to bring together their audience with engaging discussions, live streams, events, chat, courses, and payments — all in one place, all under their own brand. We’re proud to be a fully remote company of around 270 (and growing!) team members from 30+ countries around the world. We seek exceptional individuals around the world, set them up to do the best work of their lives, and in turn, create a meaningful impact in their own lives. We don't track hours, but we do manage for high expectations very closely. We collaborate across time zones, are highly async, and like to document a lot. Every year, we bring the whole company together in beautiful places around the world for our company offsites. So far, we’ve hosted offsites in Turkey, Portugal, Mexico, Thailand, Colombia, Italy, Ireland, and more, with still more to come! Check out our Careers page for more about working at Circle. About The Role The AI Quality engineering team at Circle owns the foundation for measuring, diagnosing, and improving the quality of Circle's AI-powered features. This team focuses on building the infrastructure to measure, diagnose, and improve production AI systems, rather than ML research or model training. We're looking for a Lead Engineer to help us build out the evaluation frameworks, observability tooling, and diagnostic infrastructure that tell us whether our AI Agents are working well, where to improve them, and how to make them faster and more cost-efficient. This is a hands-on player-coach role. You’ll also lead and manage the AI Quality engineering team, with an ambitious and growing roadmap. If you're excited about making AI systems work reliably, efficiently, and at scale, this is for you. What You'll Be Doing Build and own our evaluation infrastructure. Design the CI/CD pipelines, scorers, and datasets that tell us whether Circle's AI agents (planners, tool-callers, and sub-agents) are actually working, from a single tool call to a full multi-turn conversation. Diagnose exactly where quality breaks down. Trace failures across the agent pipeline including plan creation vs. execution, tool selection, tool trajectory in complex areas like workflows, site builder, and analytics. Turn what you find into prototypes that solve the issue or identify priorities for AI core engineering can help. Grow the datasets that make evaluation possible. Stand up annotation workflows and build out AI-generated and simulated conversations so we can cover more of the product faster than manual labeling alone. Run structured experiments across prompts, models, and the agent harness. Evaluate new and open-source models against our production baseline, build the framework we use to decide when to shift models, and chase cost and latency wins through model swaps, caching, and routing by plan complexity. Lead and grow the AI Quality engineering team. Set technical direction and manage day-to-day priorities, all while staying hands-on in the code yourself. Partner closely with AI Core engineering. Work with the engineers building Circle's AI products so they have real confidence that their changes are actually improving quality, not just shipping. What You'll Need To Be Successful 7+ years of experience building and shipping production software, ideally including LLM-powered agents that take real actions in a product. You've worked on complex, tool-using systems (multiple tools, planning or orchestration, sub-agents) not just simple, single-turn assistants, and you can walk us through something you shipped and how you knew it was actually working. Comfortable in Ruby on Rails / Python or ready to pick them up quickly. Ruby on Rails is our production system and the foundation that Circle’s AI Agents are built on and proficiency in Python is a strong plus, especially for the data and evaluation side of the work. Experience building evaluation or observability infrastructure for ML/AI systems. You've built eval pipelines, scorers, dashboards, or CI/CD for evals before and have experience with evaluation frameworks like Braintrust, LangSmith, or similar. Experience designing datasets, annotation workflows, or labeling pipelines for ML/AI evaluation. You know how to turn raw examples into a dataset you can trust through human annotation, AI-generated data, or simulation. Learn fast, experiment aggressively, and thrive in a highly dynamic environment. You’ll need to be comfortable running a lot of experiments and letting the results settle the argument, including the ones that don't work (which will be many of them in the beginning). Comfortable in a fast-paced environment with ambiguity. You’ll need to learn and pick up new technologies when projects require it. Strong alignment with our company values. You are proficient in English (spoken, written, and reading) at a CEFR Level C2 / ILR Level 5. Compensation & Benefits Circle offers U.S.-benchmarked compensation globally, equity in the company with ongoing refresh grants, and 35 days of paid time off each year. We’re a remote-only team that comes together twice a year for company retreats in incredible destinations around the world. Alongside incredible flexibility and autonomy, we offer a benefits package that supports health, wellbeing, and professional growth. Learn more in our Candidate Hub. Learn more Candidate Safety & Interview Process Notice Diversity, Equity & Inclusion How We Use Candidate Data Equal Employment Opportunity Visit our Candidate Hub to learn more about working at Circle, our benefits, and our hiring process. full_description: QA Engineer Key Responsibilities Own whether the platform is safe to release — the automated suite, the manual passes automation cannot replace, and the judgement about what a failing test actually means Build and keep the end-to-end suite in Playwright across the journeys that matter — a patient booked, registered, seen, billed, dispensed to and reported on — and keep it fast and trustworthy enough that nobody is tempted to ignore a red build Write the test plan for each module from what the hospital does rather than from what the screen shows, with the Business Analyst and the module owner in the room Own the regression pack that runs before every release, and grow it every time something escapes Run beta: put each release in front of the hospital's own people on migrated data, log what they find so it can be reproduced, and close it before the next release starts Be the person who says a release is not ready, and be right often enough that it carries weight Where Testing Is Mandatory Money — every path that produces a bill, a discount, a refund or a day-end total, including the ones that fail halfway through Stock — batch, expiry, issue and return, and the concurrent case where two counters sell the last strip Clinical safety — allergy and interaction checks, dose limits by age and weight, critical values, and every alert that must reach a human Access — that one hospital cannot see another's data, and that a role cannot do what it should not Integrations — a laboratory result from a real analyser, an image from a real modality, an ABHA created against the real sandbox; a mock proves the code, not the hospital Test the failure paths as seriously as the happy ones; the happy path is the one everybody already tried Beta, Parallel Run and Go-Live Turn the acceptance scripts into something the hospital's own staff can run and sign, on their own migrated data, in the beta environment Design the parallel run: what is entered in both systems, what is reconciled daily, and what "the numbers match" means for registrations, bills, collections, dispensing and reports Be on the floor through cutover and hypercare, where the real testing happens, and bring what you see back into the suite Own test data: realistic, safe, and reproducible, including the awkward records that break things — the duplicate patient, the expired batch, the refund after a partial payment Working With the Team Sit in on specification work early, because the cheapest defect is the one caught while the specification is still a paragraph Keep every defect described so that someone who was not there can reproduce it — steps, data, environment, what was expected, what happened Track what escaped and why, and bring it to the retrospective rather than to an individual Pair with engineers on the automated checks that live beside the code, so testing is not a gate at the end but a habit along the way Tech Stack Playwright · TypeScript · pytest · Python · FastAPI · PostgreSQL · SQL · REST · OpenAPI · GitHub Actions · Docker · HL7 v2 · FHIR · ABDM We build in Python on FastAPI with React in front of it, on Amazon Web Services, and we test it with Playwright and pytest. That is what this role writes, runs and reads every day, and we would rather say it plainly at the top than have you find out in week one. What you will work in every day End-to-end testing — Playwright with TypeScript, against the real web application: journeys, fixtures, test data builders, and traces that say why a run failed API and service testing — pytest and pytest-asyncio against FastAPI services; the OpenAPI schema is the contract, and tests are written to it Database verification — PostgreSQL and SQL good enough to prove in the database what the screen claims, and to spot the migration that silently rounded a rupee Continuous integration — GitHub Actions; the suite runs on every pull request, and a red build blocks a merge Environments — Docker-based environments for development, beta and UAT, each with its own reproducible data set Performance — load testing at peak outpatient volume with k6 or Locust, and the judgement to know which number matters Integration test beds — HL7 v2 messages from analysers over MLLP, DICOM modality worklist and PACS, and the ABDM sandbox for ABHA creation and consent Defect and test management — a shared tracker visible to the hospital, with a published severity and response standard What we need you to have used in production Playwright, Cypress or Selenium on a system people depended on — writing maintainable tests, not recording brittle ones A programming language, enough to write helpers, fixtures and data builders; TypeScript or Python, and the other within the first month API testing at the service layer, and the sense to know which layer a case belongs at SQL to verify data directly, not only through the screen A CI pipeline your tests ran in, where a failure meant something to the team Good to have as well Healthcare, banking, insurance, or another domain where a wrong number is a real consequence Testing integrations with devices or external systems — an analyser, a payment gateway, a government API Test design beyond the checklist: boundaries, equivalence classes, state transitions, concurrency Accessibility and usability testing on screens used by people who did not choose the software Running a user acceptance test with non-technical staff, and getting it signed Security testing basics — role-based access, injection, the OWASP top ten — and reading a VAPT report What You'll Bring Three or more years in software quality with real ownership of automation, not only manual execution Have been the person who said a release was not ready, and can describe what you saw and what happened next Enough programming to be useful in a codebase: helpers, fixtures, test data, and the occasional fix to the thing you found Comfortable at the service layer and in the database, not only at the screen Can write a defect report that a developer reproduces first time, and a test plan that a module owner recognises as their own work Methodical about the awkward cases — the refund after a partial payment, the expired batch, the patient registered twice — because those are where a hospital gets hurt Willing to sit at a billing counter or beside a nurse for a shift and come back with the cases the specification missed Preferred: healthcare or another domain where correctness is auditable after the fact, and experience with a parallel run or a system cutover

In this hands-on engineering role, you will turn the latest advancements in generative artificial intelligence into resilient, scalable business solutions. You will specialize in constructing Advanced Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipelines, engineering autonomous agents with deterministic tool-calling capabilities, optimizing prompt workflows, experimenting with parameter-efficient model adaptation (LoRA/QLoRA), and serving high-performance inference APIs via containerized microservices hosted on AWS or Microsoft Azure. Key Responsibilities A. RAG Architecture & Vector Search Engineering RAG Pipeline Development: Design and implement end-to-end RAG pipelines incorporating multi-modal document parsing, recursive text splitting, and semantic chunking. Vector Store Management: Integrate, optimize, and benchmark vector databases (Pinecone, Qdrant, Chroma, Weaviate, pgvector, Azure AI Search) for sub-second similarity search. Hybrid Search & Re-ranking: Implement hybrid retrieval combining dense vector embeddings with sparse lexical keyword matching (BM25) and cross-encoder re-ranking models (Cohere Rerank, BGE). Context Optimization: Engineer contextual compression, parent-document retrieval, and metadata filtering schemas to eliminate context noise and hallucinations. B. Agentic Workflows & Multi-Tool Integration Agentic Frameworks: Build stateful multi-agent workflows and autonomous task execution loops using LangChain, LangGraph, LlamaIndex, or AutoGen. Tool Calling & Action APIs: Develop robust, type-safe function-calling and tool-use interfaces connecting LLMs to external REST APIs, relational databases, and enterprise systems. Loop Safeguards & Routing: Implement plan-and-solve agent patterns, multi-step reflection loops, and fallback error-handling to prevent infinite agent recursion. C. Prompt Engineering, Output Validation & Fine-Tuning Prompt Engineering: Design and test systematic prompt templates utilizing Chain-of-Thought (CoT), Few-Shot prompting, ReAct patterns, and directional stimulus prompting. Structured Output Parsing: Enforce deterministic, validated output structures using Pydantic, Instructor, Guidance, or Outlines to guarantee reliable downstream ingestion. Model Adaptation: Conduct Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT, LoRA, QLoRA) on open-weights models (Llama 3, Mistral, Phi-3/4) for domain-specific tasks. D. Backend API & Inference Microservices Inference APIs (FastAPI): Develop high-throughput asynchronous backend microservices using Python (FastAPI), managing connection pooling, concurrency, and rate limiting. Streaming Latency: Implement low-latency streaming inference pipelines utilizing Server-Sent Events (SSE) and WebSockets for conversational user interfaces. Inference Engines: Optimize inference throughput utilizing modern serving engines like vLLM, TensorRT-LLM, or Ollama, minimizing Time-to-First-Token (TTFT). Containerized Deployment: Containerize applications with Docker and configure deployment manifests for Kubernetes, AWS ECS/EKS, or Azure Container Apps. E. full_description: About the Role: GSK’s Enterprise AI team builds AI solutions that prove value fast and scale to production. The Forward Deployed Engineer is the engineer GSK sends in to find out whether an AI idea will work — embedded with business unit teams, proving ideas through PoCs, PoVs, and MVPs at a days-to-weeks cadence, then handing the proven solution off to the Sr. Solutions Engineer for scale-up. The pattern is proven by AI-native companies — Anthropic, Palantir, OpenAI — and this role brings that model to GSK. This senior engineer role embeds directly with business unit teams — product owners, engineering leads, and the wider BU — to understand the problem and execute. Most prototyping work is AI-augmented: AI coding assistants and multi-agent workflows handle the bulk of routine coding, freeing the FDE to focus on framing, judgement, and validation. The role works directly inside the customer’s business and emerges with working software and a defensible value hypothesis — not slideware. The FDE does not carry use cases through to long-term operations — clean handoff to the Sr. Solutions Engineer is part of the role. Why This Role Exists: Enterprise AI’s impact depends on engineers who can close the gap between what AI can do and what the business needs — fast, embedded, and without requiring the business to specify everything upfront. The FDE is that engineer. Proves AI ideas fast — shipping working prototypes at days-to-weeks cadence before significant investment is committed. Works directly inside the business — not at arm’s length — building the trust and domain understanding that separate useful AI from academic AI. Builds the organisation’s reusable AI engineering assets — every engagement distilled into patterns, agents, and reference architectures the whole team benefits from. Contribute reusable agents, prompt templates, and reference architectures to the organisation’s pattern library after each engagement.
